akhfash:3-3.t: He said: ﴿وَأَذَانٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ﴿أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَرِيۤءٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, i.e. "بأَنّ اللهَ بريء" (that Allah is free of …); and likewise ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخْزِي ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [2], i.e. "بأَن الله".

akhfash:5-5.t:
He said: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ﴾: He used the plural of paucity because its meaning is "the four". That is because "الأَشْهُر" is used only when "three" to "ten" is mentioned with it; when "three" to "ten" is not mentioned, it is "الشُّهُورُ".
And He said ﴿وَٱقْعُدُواْ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾, dropping "على" (on). The poet said [in the wāfir metre, and it is the fifty-sixth poetic witness]:
نُغالِى اللَّحْمَ للأَضْيافِ نِيْئاً * وَنَبْذُلُه إذا نَضِجَ القُدُورُ
(We pay dearly for meat for our guests while it is raw, and give it freely when the pots are cooked.)
He meant: "نُغالِى باللحم" (we pay dearly for the meat).

akhfash:6-6.t:
He said: ﴿وَأَنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ﴾. [Translator's note: the source prints «وَأَنْ»; the Qur'anic text has «وَإِنْ».] He began a nominal clause after (أنْ), though making أحد nominative by an implied verb is the more analogical of the two ways, because a nominal clause does not begin after the particles of condition. However, they have said that with "أَنْ" because of its firm standing and its elegance when nouns follow it and there is no verb after it that is overtly jussive, as [the poet] said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the one hundred and seventy-eighth poetic witness]:
* عاوِدْ هَراةَ وأَنْ مَعْمُورُها خَرِبا *
(Return to Herat, even if its inhabited part has become ruined.)
And [another] said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-fourth poetic witness]:
لا تَجْزَعِي أَنْ مُنْفِساً أَهْلَكْتُهُ * وأَذا هَلَكْتُ فَعِنْدَ ذلِكَ فَاجْزَعي
(Do not grieve if I have squandered something precious; but when I perish, then grieve.)
They have claimed that the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-fifth poetic witness]:
أَتَجْزَعُ أَنْ نَفْسٌ أَتَاهَا حِمامُها * فَهَلاَّ الَّتِي عَنْ بينِ جَنْبَيْكَ تَدْفَعُ
(Do you grieve that a soul has met its death? Why then do you not defend the one between your own two sides?)
are recited only with the nominative, the verb having fallen on something connected with it. Here a nominal clause has begun after "أنْ"; and if you wish, you may make it nominative by an implied verb.

akhfash:7-7.t: He said: ﴿كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَعِندَ رَسُولِهِ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ﴾: this is an exception excluded from the beginning of the speech, and (الذينَ) is in the position of the accusative.

akhfash:8-8.t: He said: ﴿كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ لاَ يَرْقُبُواْ فِيكُمْ﴾: He left something implied, as though [He said] "How will you not fight them?", and Allah knows best.

akhfash:12-12.t: He said: ﴿وَإِن نَّكَثُوۤاْ أَيْمَانَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ﴾; He said ﴿فَقَاتِلُوۤاْ أَئِمَّةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾: he made the hamza a yāʾ because it is in a position of kasra and what precedes it has fatḥa, and he did not pronounce the hamza because two hamzas come together. Whoever holds that two hamzas may be combined pronounces the hamza.

akhfash:13-13.t: He said: ﴿وَهَمُّواْ بِإِخْرَاجِ ٱلرَّسُولِ﴾, because you say "هَمَمْتُ بكذا" (I intended such-and-such) and "أَهَمَّني كذا" (such-and-such concerned me).

akhfash:25-25.t: He said: ﴿فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾: it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). Likewise every plural whose third letter is alif, followed after the alif by a doubled letter or by two or more light letters, is a diptote both when definite and when indefinite, such as "محاريب", "تماثيل", "مساجد" and the like — unless it ends in hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa); if it ends in hāʾ, it is triptote when indefinite, such as "طيالِسَة" and "صياقِلَة". The Arabs prevented this plural from being declined only because it is a pattern that does not occur for a singular and occurs only for the plural, and the plural is heavier than the singular; so since this pattern occurs only for what is heavier, it was not declined. As for the one ending in hāʾ, it is declined because the hāʾ is separable, as though it were a noun on its own; and declension falls only at the end of the noun, so it fell on the hāʾ, and that is why it is declined. It was likened to "حَضْرَموت", and "حَضْرَمَوْتَ" is declined when indefinite.

akhfash:28-28.t: He said: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾, which is "الفَقْر" (poverty). You say "عالَ" "يَعِيلُ" "عَيْلَةً", i.e. "he became poor". And "أَعَالَ" "إِعالَةً": when he came to have dependants. And "عالَ عِيالَهُ" (he supported his dependants) and "هو يَعُولُهم" "عَوْلاً" and "عِيَالَةً". And He said "﴿ذٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَعُولُواْ﴾, i.e. that you not have to support dependants. And "أعالَ الرجلُ" "يُعِيلُ" when he comes to have dependants.

akhfash:30-30.t: [And He said:] ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ﴾. Some dropped the tanwīn, and that is poor, because the tanwīn is left out only when the noun can do without "ابن" (son) and is traced to a well-known name. Here the noun cannot do without it: if you said "وَقَالَتِ اليَهودُ عَزَيْزُ" it would not be a complete statement. However, it has been read so, and frequently, and we read it so by way of quotation (ḥikāya), as though they meant "وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ نَبِيُّنا عُزَيْزُ ابنُ اللهِ" (the Jews said: our prophet ʿUzayr is the son of Allah). [Translator's note: the source alternates between «عزير» and «عزيز»; translated as written.]

akhfash:32-32.t: He said: ﴿وَيَأْبَىٰ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ﴾*, because (أن يتم) is a noun [an interpreted maṣdar], as though it were "يَأبَى اللهُ أَلاَّ إِتمامَ نُورِه" (Allah refuses anything but the completion of His light).

akhfash:34-35.t:
He said: ﴿يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ﴾, then He said ﴿يُحْمَىٰ عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, so He made the speech refer to the last of them. The poet said [in the munsariḥ metre, and it is the sixtieth poetic witness]:
نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وَأَنْتَ بِما * عِنْدَكَ راضٍ والرَأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)

akhfash:37-37.t:
He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾: it is postponement. You say "أَنْسَأْتُهُ الدَّيْنَ" when you have left it to him to defer. And "نَسَأْتُ عَنْهُ دَيْنَهُ", i.e. I deferred his debt for him. I only said "أَنْسَأْتُهُ الدَّيْنَ" because you say "I made it his to defer", and "نَسَأْتُ عَنْهُ دَيْنَه" "فَأَنَا أنَّسَؤُهُ", i.e. I defer it. Likewise "النَّساءُ في العُمْر" (prolongation of life); it is said: "مَنْ سَرَّهُ النَّساءُ في العُمُر" (whoever would be pleased to have his life prolonged …). And one says "عِرْق النَّسَا" (the sciatic vein) without hamza.
And He said ﴿لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ﴾, because it is from "وَاطَأْتُ" (I agreed with). Like it is (هِيَ أَشَدُّ وِطاءً), i.e. "مواطأة" (accord), which is concordance. Some read (وَطْءا), i.e. standing firm.

akhfash:38-38.t: He said: ﴿ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, because it is from "تَثاقَلْتُمْ"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the thāʾ, so it became quiescent, and an alif was introduced for it so as to begin the speech with it.

akhfash:40-40.t:
He said: ﴿وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلْعُلْيَا﴾, because He did not construe it with (جَعَلَ) but construed it as a mubtadaʾ.
And He said ﴿ثَانِيَ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, and likewise (ثالثُ ثلاثةٍ, the third of three); this is the speech of the Arabs. "ثاني واحدٍ" (making one into two) and "ثالثُ اثْنَينِ" (making two into three) are also permissible. In the Book of Allah: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلاَثَةٍ إِلاَّ هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ وَلاَ خَمْسَةٍ إِلاَّ هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ﴾; and He said ﴿ثَلاثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾, ﴿خَمْسَةٌ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ and ﴿سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:41-41.t: He said: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾, in this ḥāl (circumstance). If you wish, (انفِروا) in the dialect of those who say "يَنْفِر", and if you wish, (انْفُرُوا).

akhfash:43-43.t: He said: ﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ﴾, because it is a question, i.e. "for what reason?".

akhfash:46-46.t: He said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن كَرِهَ ٱللَّهُ ٱنبِعَاثَهُمْ﴾, deriving it from "بَعَثْتُهُ" (I roused him), so "انْبَعَثَ" (he was roused). I have heard from the Arabs someone say: "لَوْ دُعِينا لانْدَعَيْنا" (had we been called, we would have responded). You say: "انْبَعَثَ انَبِعاثاً", i.e. "I roused him" so "he was roused, a rousing". And you say "انْقُطِعَ بِهِ" when he speaks and breaks down, and you do not say "قُطِعَ بِهِ".

akhfash:57-57.t:
He said: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَئاً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلاً﴾, because it is from "اِدَّخَلَ" "يَدَّخِلُ". Some read (مَدْخَلا), deriving it from "دَخَلَ" "يَدْخُل", and to my knowledge it is the poorer of the two ways. They mention that in the reading of Ubayy it is (مُنْدَخَلاً), meaning one thing after another. He said ﴿مُغَارَاتٍ﴾ only because it is from "أَغَارَ", so the place is "مُغارٌ". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the one hundred and seventy-first poetic witness]:
الحمدُ للهِ مُمْسانَا وَمُصْبَحَنا * بِالخَيْرِ صَبْحَنا رَبِّي وَمَسَّانا
(Praise be to Allah at our evening and our morning; with good has my Lord granted us morning and evening.)
because they are from "أَمْسَى" and "أَصْبَحَ". When you pause on "مَلْجَأ" you say "مَلْجَأَا", because it is an accusative with tanwīn, so you pause with alif, as in your saying "رأيتُ زيدَا".

akhfash:58-58.t: He said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ﴾, and some read (يَلْمُزُكَ).

akhfash:61-61.t:
He said: ﴿قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. he is an ear of good, not an ear of evil. Some read (أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ), but the first is the better of the two, because if you said "هو أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُم" it would not be as good as (هو أَذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُم); this is permissible on condition that you make (لكم) an adjective of "الأُذُنْ".
And He said ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِنكُمْ﴾, i.e. "and he is a mercy".
And He said ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. he believes them, just as you say of a man "أَنَا ما يُؤمِنُ لي بأَنْ أَقُولَ كذا وكذا", i.e. he does not believe me.

akhfash:62-62.t:
He said: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ لِيُرْضُوكُمْ﴾ and "سَيَحْلِفُوَن بالله لَكُمِ لِيُرْضُوكُمْ"; I understand it only as meaning "لَيُرضُنَّكُم" (they will surely please you), as the poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-sixth poetic witness]:
إِذا قُلْتُ قَدْنِي قالَ باللهِ حِلْفَةً * لَتُغِنِيَ عَنّي ذا أَنائِكَ أَجْمَعا
(Whenever I say "Enough for me!", he says, swearing an oath by Allah: "You shall surely empty this vessel of yours entirely for me.")
i.e. "لَتُغْنِيَنَّ عني". It is like ﴿وَلِتَصْغَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e. "ولتُصْغِيَنَّ".

akhfash:63-63.t: He said: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّهُ مَن يُحَادِدِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ﴾: he gave the alif kasra because what follows the fāʾ that is the apodosis of the conditional begins anew.

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿فَرِحَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلاَفَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. "مُخالَفَةً" (in opposition). Some read (خَلْفَ, behind); (خِلافَ) is the more correct of the two because they opposed, like "قَاتَلُوا قِتالا", and because it is the maṣdar of "خَالَفُوا".

akhfash:90-90.t: He said: ﴿وَجَآءَ ٱلْمُعَذِرُونَ﴾, light, because it is from "اَعْذَرُوا". Some read (المُعَذِّرُونَ), doubled, meaning "المُعْتَذرُونَ" (those offering excuses), but the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl, as He said ﴿يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾; and that is how we read. It may be (المُعِذِّرُون) with kasra on the ʿayn because of the meeting of two quiescents; [Translator's note: the source prints «المُعْذِرُون», but the context requires kasra on the ʿayn.] it was given fatḥa only because the fatḥa of the tāʾ was transferred to it. The ʿayn may also take ḍamma, following the mīm; this is like (المُرْدِفِين).

akhfash:98-98.t:
He said: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾, just as you say "هذا رَجُل السَّوْءِ" (this is the man of evil). The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-seventh poetic witness]:
وَكُنْتَ كَذِئْبِ السَّوْءِ لَمَّا رَأَى دَماً	* بِصاحِبِه يَوْماً أَحارَ عَلَى الدَّمِ
(You were like the wicked wolf: when one day it saw blood on its companion, it turned upon the blood.)
It has been read (دائِرَةُ السُّوءِ), and this is weak; [Translator's note: the reasoning that follows seems rather to favour «السُّوء» in this phrase; translated as written.] for when you say "كانت عليهم دائرة السُوءِ" it is better than "رجل السَوْءِ". Do you not see that you say "كانت عليهم دائرة الهزيمة" (the turn of defeat was upon them)? For "the man" is not annexed to "evil" as this is annexed, since this is explained by good and evil, as we say "سلكتُ طريقَ الشرَ" (I took the path of evil) and "تركتُ طريقَ الخَيْر" (I abandoned the path of good).

akhfash:100-100.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنْصَارِ﴾. Some read (والأَنْصارُ) in the nominative, conjoining it to His words (والسَّابِقُونَ); but the right way is the genitive, because the first forerunners were from both groups together.

akhfash:102-102.t: He said: ﴿خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً﴾. In Arabic it may be [in the sense of] "بآخرَ" (with another), just as you say "اِسْتَوىَ الماءُ والخَشَبَةَ" (the water rose level with the post), i.e. "بالخَشَبَةِ", and "خَلَطْتُ الماءَ واللَّبَنَ" (I mixed the water and the milk), i.e. "بِالَّلبَنِ" (with the milk).

akhfash:103-103.t: He said: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾. His words ﴿وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾ are a new beginning (ʿalā al-ibtidāʾ); or, if you wish, you may make it an adjective (ṣifa) of "الصدقة" (alms) and then bring بها as emphasis (tawkīd). Likewise (تُطَهِّرُهُم).

akhfash:106-106.t: He said: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ﴾, because it is from "أَرْجَأْتُ". Some read (مُرْجَوْنَ) in the dialect of those who say (أَرْجَيْتُ). [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; one of them is presumably the hamzated «مُرْجَؤُونَ».]

akhfash:108-108.t: He said: ﴿أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ﴾: He means "مُنْذُ أوَّلِ يَوْمٍ" (since the first day), because some Arabs say "لَمْ أَرَهُ مِنْ يَوْمِ كَذا" (I have not seen him from such-and-such a day), meaning "since the first day"; by it he means "from the first of the days", like your saying "لَقِيتُ كُلَّ رَجُلٍ" (I met every man), by which you mean "كُلَّ الرِجّال" (all the men).

akhfash:109-109.t: He said: ﴿هَارٍ فَٱنْهَارَ بِهِ﴾. They mentioned that it is from "يَهُورُ" and is metathesised; its origin is "هائِرٌ"*, but it was metathesised just as "شاكِ السِّلاح" (bristling with weapons) was, [and] it is really "شائِك".

akhfash:110-110.t: He said: ﴿رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ﴾, and (تَقَطَّعَ) in the reading of some; and all are good. [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; the variant is presumably «تُقَطَّعَ».]

akhfash:112-112.t: He said: ﴿ٱلتَّائِبُونَ ٱلْعَابِدُونَ..﴾ to the end of the verse, then explained (وَبَشِّرِ المُؤْمِنِينَ); because His words — and Allah knows best — (التائبون) are only an explanation of His words ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ﴾; then He explained and said: "they are those who repent".

akhfash:113-113.t: Then He said: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾; he says: "and they were not to seek forgiveness for the polytheists". And He said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تُؤْمِنَ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. faith was not for it except by Allah's leave.

akhfash:114-114.t: He said: ﴿إِلاَّ عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ﴾: He means "إلاَّ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْعِدَةٍ" (except after a promise), just as you say: "ما كان هذا الشرُّ إلاَّ عَنْ قَوْلٍ كانَ بَيَنْكَمُا" (this trouble came only from words that passed between you two), i.e. it came about from that.

akhfash:117-117.t: He said: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ﴾, and some read (تَزِيغُ). He put an implied noun in (كادَ) and (كادَت), and made "القلوب" nominative by (تَزِيغُ). If you wish you may make it nominative by (كادَ) and make (تَزِيغُ) a ḥāl (circumstantial); or, if you wish, you may treat it as resembling "كانَ", implying a noun in (كادَ) and putting (تَزِيغُ قلوبُ) in the position of the khabar (predicate).

akhfash:118-118.t: He said: ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَن لاَّ مَلْجَأَ﴾: it is like this when you pause on it, and you do not say (ملجأ ا), because there is no nūn [tanwīn] here. Do you not see that if you paused on "لا خَوْفَ" you would not add an alif? As for "لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأَا", pausing on it is with alif because the accusative in it has tanwīn.

akhfash:123-123.t: He said: ﴿وَلِيَجِدُواْ فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً﴾, and that is how we read; some read (غُلْظَةَ). They are two dialects.

akhfash:124-124.t: He said: ﴿أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَـٰذِهِ إِيمَاناً﴾: "أيّ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the verb has fallen on the hāʾ. If you say: "Why not imply a verb at its beginning, as He said ﴿أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً﴾?" — it is because before "بشر" there is an interrogative particle, which has more claim to a verb, whereas (أيّ) makes the interrogative particle unnecessary, so nothing with more claim to a verb comes before it; so it became like your saying "زيدٌ ضَرْبتُه" (Zayd, I struck him). Whoever puts "زيداً ضربُته" in the accusative in a statement would put "أيّ" in the accusative here.

akhfash:127-127.t: He said: ﴿نَّظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ﴾. It is as though He said "some of them said to others", because their looking in this place was a gesture or something like it; and Allah knows best.

akhfash:128-128.t: He said: ﴿عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾: He made (ما) a noun and (عَنِتُّم) part of its ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:61-61.t:
﴿وَمِنْهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the wāw is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّبِيَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو أذن خير", and خير is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is likewise the object of the saying. The clause قل هو أذن.. is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to خير before them. ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and the clause is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أذن. The clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ conjoined to أذن.
﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to رحمة. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿يُؤْذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿رَسُولَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar.
﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt. The nominal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:62-62.t:
﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ and ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿لِيُرْضُوكُمْ﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the implied أن after the lām of causation and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يحلفون. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿أَحَقُّ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾
the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, i.e. "Allah is more entitled to being pleased". ﴿أَنْ﴾ a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive (jāzim). [Translator's note: the source vocalizes the word here as أَنْ; the Quranic text reads إِنْ.] ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its subject (ism). ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the clause كانوا is an initial clause, the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).

daas-irab:63-63.t:
﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and لم is a particle of negation, jussive-making and tense-reversal. ﴿يَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ أنّ, and the hāʾ is its ism (subject). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يُحادِدِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he". ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿فَأَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿أن﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to its omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿نارَ﴾ its ism. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a proper name and foreign (a diptote). ﴿خالِداً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the active participle ﴿خالِداً﴾. The nominal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنه. The clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. And أنه with its khabar takes the place of the two objects of يعلموا. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām denotes distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿الْخِزْيُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ naʿt (adjective). The clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:64-64.t:
﴿يَحْذَرُ الْمُنافِقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the subjunctive-making أن and the verb after it, interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "the sending down of a sura". ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿تُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is its object; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "she/it". ﴿بِما﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, i.e. "of what is established in their hearts". The verbal clause is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of the sura. ﴿قُلِ﴾ an imperative verb, the fāʿil is "you", and the clause is resumptive. ﴿اسْتَهْزِؤُا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ﴾ inna, its ism (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the active participle مخرج, and the clause ﴿تَحْذَرُونَ﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause إن الله مخرج is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:65-65.t:
﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive. The lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is conditional. ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm marks the masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ the lām links the answer of the oath. ﴿يقولن﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been deleted to avoid a succession of identical letters; the deleted wāw is in the position of nominative as fāʿil, and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. The clause has no grammatical position, being the answer of the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted since the answer of the oath indicates it. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its ism (subject), and the clause ﴿نَخُوضُ﴾ is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause إنما كنا.. is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَنَلْعَبُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَبِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb تستهزئون, and the hamza is interrogative.
﴿وَآياتِهِ﴾ a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ a conjoined noun. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna; the tāʾ is its ism and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural.
﴿تَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم تستهزئون.. is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:66-66.t:
﴿لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ لا of prohibition and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The clause is resumptive.
﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil and the mīm marks the masculine plural; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿إِيمانِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿نَعْفُ﴾ the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the weak letter, which is the wāw; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we". ﴿عَنْ طائِفَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طائفة. The clause of the protasis is initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿نُعَذِّبْ﴾ the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive. ﴿طائِفَةٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive-making condition not joined to the fāʾ or the surprise إذا. [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿طائِفَةٍ﴾ here with kasra; as a mafʿūl bihi it is accusative (طائِفَةً) in the Quranic text.] ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ أنّ, and the hāʾ is its ism (subject). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna, and the wāw is its ism, and ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ is its khabar (predicate). The clause كانوا مجرمين is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of أنهم. And أنّ with its ism and khabar is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb نعذب.

daas-irab:67-67.t:
﴿الْمُنافِقُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالْمُنافِقاتُ﴾ a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun. ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ a second mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to its omitted khabar (predicate). The nominal clause بعضهم من بعض is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ المنافقون. The clause المنافقون بعضهم من بعض is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَأْمُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالْمُنْكَرِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise the clauses after it.. The clause ﴿فَنَسِيَهُمْ﴾ is conjoined.
﴿إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ inna and its ism (subject). ﴿هُمُ﴾ a nominative pronoun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْفاسِقُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause هم الفاسقون is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. The clause إن المنافقين is causal, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:68-68.t:
﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالْمُنافِقاتِ﴾ a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural.
﴿وَالْكُفَّارَ﴾ a conjoined noun. ﴿نارَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), a foreign proper noun. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to خالدين. ﴿هِيَ﴾ a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حَسْبُهُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl. ﴿وَلَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُقِيمٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective), and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:69-69.t:
﴿كَالَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), i.e. "you are like those who"; or the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), khabar: "you are like those who".. And ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, i.e. "like those who passed before you". ﴿كانُوا أَشَدَّ﴾ kāna, its ism (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the elative noun أشد. ﴿قُوَّةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَأَكْثَرَ﴾ conjoined to أشد. ﴿أَمْوالًا﴾ tamyīz. ﴿وَأَوْلاداً﴾ conjoined. ﴿فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿بِخَلاقِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf); likewise the clause ﴿فَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِخَلاقِكُمْ﴾. ﴿كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-forming ما and the past verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "an enjoyment being like the enjoyment of those before you". ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿بِخَلاقِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to استمتع. ﴿وَخُضْتُمْ كَالَّذِي﴾ i.e. "like those who"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq; the clause is conjoined, and the clause ﴿خاضُوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ﴾ is the khabar; the nominal clause أولئك حبطت أعمالهم is resumptive. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْخاسِرُونَ﴾ khabar.

daas-irab:70-70.t:
﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is interrogative. ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle of negation, jussive-making and tense-reversal. ﴿يَأْتِهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the weak letter, which is the yāʾ. The hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the mīm marks the masculine plural. ﴿نَبَأُ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿قَوْمِ﴾ badal (substitute) of الذين, genitive with the kasra. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَعادٍ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾ a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun, genitive with the fatḥa, a diptote because it is a proper name and foreign. ﴿وَقَوْمِ﴾ a conjoined noun. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa, also because it is a proper name and foreign. ﴿وَأَصْحابِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿مَدْيَنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive — رسلهم: fāʿil — with the fatḥa because it is a diptote. [Translator's note: the words «رسلهم: فاعل» appear misplaced inside this sentence in the source; the parsing of رسلهم is given again below.] ﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتِ﴾ conjoined. The clause ﴿أَتَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ﴾ is resumptive. ﴿رُسُلُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil, and ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿كانَ اللَّهُ﴾ kāna, and the Name of Majesty is its ism (subject). ﴿لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the implied أن after the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; or the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb after it is in the position of genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e. "Allah was not intending to wrong them". The clause فما كان..
is conjoined. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk), and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its ism. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi of the verb ﴿يَظْلِمُونَ﴾, and the clause يظلمون is in the position of accusative as khabar; the clause كانوا is conjoined.

daas-irab:71-71.t:
This verse closely resembles verse 68 in its i'rab. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the verbal clause ﴿سَيَرْحَمُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar (predicate). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ inna, its ism (subject) and its two khabars, and the clause is causal, with no grammatical position.
The nominal clause أولئك is resumptive.

daas-irab:72-72.t:
﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, and the verbal clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to خالدين. ﴿وَمَساكِنَ﴾ conjoined to جنات. ﴿طَيِّبَةً﴾ naʿt. ﴿فِي جَنَّاتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted second naʿt of جنات. ﴿عَدْنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَرِضْوانٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it is qualified, and the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ are attached to this omitted naʿt; the wāw is resumptive. ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause ﴿رِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ... ﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached pronoun, second mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ its khabar. ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ naʿt, and the clause هو الفوز.. is the khabar of the demonstrative; the nominal clause ذلك هو.. is resumptive.

daas-irab:73-73.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ يا is a vocative particle; أيّ is an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the one addressed (munādā). ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ an imperative verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is initial. ﴿وَالْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ conjoined to الكفار. The clause ﴿اغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ is conjoined to the clause جاهد الكفار. ﴿وَمَأْواهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif owing to impossibility; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation, the mīm marks the masculine plural, and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿جَهَنَّمُ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَبِئْسَ﴾ an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "بئس المصير مصيرهم", and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:74-74.t: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ after it are attached (mutaʿalliq); the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the answer of the oath. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a preposition of oath. The lām occurs in the answer of the implied oath "أقسم والله". [Translator's note: in the Quranic text this wāw precedes the lām of an omitted oath; the source's wording is translated as written.] ﴿لَقَدْ ... ﴾ قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq), and the clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the answer of the oath. ﴿كَلِمَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْكُفْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَكَفَرُوا﴾ conjoined. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to the verb كفروا. ﴿إِسْلامِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the verbal clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهَمُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِما﴾ ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿لَمْ﴾ jussive-making. ﴿يَنالُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما is negating, and the clause ﴿نَقَمُوا﴾ is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle. ﴿أَغْناهُمُ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif owing to impossibility, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of genitive by a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb نقموا. ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to أغناهم. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ إن is a jussive-making conditional particle, and the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿يَتُوبُوا﴾ the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, and its fāʿil. ﴿يَكُ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn that has been deleted for lightening; its ism (subject) is omitted, i.e. "the matter would be ﴿خَيْراً﴾ for them". ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to خير. The clause of the protasis has no grammatical position, being initial, and the clause of the apodosis likewise has no grammatical position because it is not linked by the fāʾ or the surprise إذا. And ﴿فَإِنْ يَتُوبُوا.. يُعَذِّبْهُمُ﴾ is parsed like the preceding. [Translator's note: the Quranic text here reads ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَوَلَّوْا يُعَذِّبْهُمُ﴾; the source's quotation is translated as written.] ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the two are attached to يعذبهم. ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ما is negating. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿وَلِيٍّ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَلا نَصِيرٍ﴾ a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun. And في الأرض: the two are also attached to an omitted khabar.

daas-irab:75-75.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the wāw is resumptive. مَن is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). The nominal clause is resumptive, and the clause ﴿عاهَدَ اللَّهَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). ﴿إن﴾ conditional. ﴿آتانا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif owing to impossibility, and ﴿نا﴾ is its object; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he". The preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ are attached to the verb, and the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is initial. ﴿لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath, and the clause has no grammatical position, being the answer of the oath. ﴿وَلَنَكُونَنَّ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa; its ism (subject) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:76-76.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿لما﴾ adverbial and conditional, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb بخلوا. ﴿آتاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿بَخِلُوا﴾ the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, and the clause ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ is conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial), after the circumstantial wāw.

daas-irab:77-77.t:
﴿فَأَعْقَبَهُمْ﴾ a past verb; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿نِفاقاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (نفاقا). ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾ the two are attached to another omitted naʿt, i.e. "a hypocrisy established in their hearts, extending to the day they meet Him". ﴿يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿بِما﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdar-forming; together with the verb ﴿أَخْلَفُوا﴾ after it, it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb أعقبهم, i.e. "that ensued for them because of their breaking the promise and their lying". ﴿بما وعدوه﴾ ما and the verb وعدوه after it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as second mafʿūl bihi of أخلف. ما can also be parsed as a relative noun in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi ... and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. [Translator's note: the source writes ﴿بما وعدوه﴾; the Quranic text reads ﴿مَا وَعَدُوهُ﴾.] ﴿وَبِما كانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined, and the clause يكذبون is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb كانوا.

daas-irab:78-78.t:
﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation and disapproval. ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle of negation, jussive-making and tense-reversal. ﴿يَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm). ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its ism (subject), and the clause ﴿يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ﴾ is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as its khabar (predicate). ﴿وَنَجْواهُمْ﴾ conjoined to سرهم, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif owing to impossibility. The hāʾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation, and أنّ with its ism and khabar takes the place of the two objects of يعلموا.
﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ﴾ أنّ, its ism and its khabar. ﴿الْغُيُوبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the nominal clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:79-79.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَلْمِزُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. And ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from المؤمنين. [Translator's note: so in the source; the ḥāl presumably refers to المطوعين.] ﴿فِي الصَّدَقاتِ﴾ the two are attached to يلمزون. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a noun conjoined to المطوعين, in the position of accusative. ﴿لا يَجِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and لا is negating. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿جُهْدَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. The clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; منهم: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of الذين at the beginning of the verse. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:80-80.t:
﴿اسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ jussive-making lā of prohibition. ﴿تَسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive-making conditional particle that makes two imperfect verbs jussive. ﴿تَسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿سَبْعِينَ﴾ an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the nūn compensates for the tanwīn of the singular noun. ﴿مَرَّةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿فَلَنْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿لن﴾ a subjunctive-making particle. ﴿يَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to يغفر, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the clause of the protasis ﴿إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ..﴾ is initial. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām denotes distance and the kāf is a particle of address. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ أنّ, and the hāʾ is its ism (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنهم. And أنّ with its ism and khabar is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ is its khabar; the nominal clause والله لا يهدي ... is resumptive.

daas-irab:81-81.t:
﴿فَرِحَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْمُخَلَّفُونَ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw, a sound masculine plural. ﴿بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿خِلافَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to مقعد. ﴿رَسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, and the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَرِهُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the subjunctive-making ﴿أَنْ﴾ and the verb ﴿يُجاهِدُوا﴾ after it is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "and they disliked striving". ﴿بِأَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ conjoined. في سبيل الله: the two are attached to the verb, and the verbal clause is conjoined; likewise the clause قالوا. ﴿لا تَنْفِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿فِي الْحَرِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. ﴿نارُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a proper name and foreign. ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ khabar (predicate).
﴿حَرًّا﴾ tamyīz (specification). The nominal clause is a mafʿūl bihi, the object of the saying. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its ism (subject), and the clause ﴿يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ is its khabar. The clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is initial, with no grammatical position. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if they understood.. they would not have rejoiced".

daas-irab:82-82.t: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of command, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿بِما﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun) جزاء. Or ما is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its ism (subject), and the clause ﴿يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

daas-irab:83-83.t:
﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional. ﴿رَجَعَكَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿إِلى طائِفَةٍ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طائفة, and the clause is initial. ﴿فَاسْتَأْذَنُوكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلْخُرُوجِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لَنْ﴾ a subjunctive-making particle. ﴿تَخْرُجُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿مَعِيَ﴾ an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person; the yāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time, also attached to the verb تخرجوا. The verbal clause is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The verbal clause ﴿وَلَنْ تُقاتِلُوا ... ﴾ is conjoined.
﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ inna and its ism (subject). ﴿رَضِيتُمْ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿بِالْقُعُودِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أَوَّلَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to the verb. ﴿مَرَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَاقْعُدُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition). ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to the verb. ﴿الْخالِفِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the verbal clause has no grammatical position, being the answer of a non-jussive conditional إذا. The clause إنكم رضيتم is causal, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:84-84.t:
﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لا is the jussive-making lā of prohibition. ﴿تُصَلِّ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the weak letter, which is the yāʾ.
﴿عَلى أَحَدٍ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أحد. ﴿ماتَ﴾ the clause is a naʿt of أحد. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time attached to the verb. The clause لا تصل is resumptive.
﴿وَلا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ﴾ conjoined to لا تصل على أحد.. The nominal clause ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا﴾ is causal, with no grammatical position.
﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its ism (subject), and the clause كفروا is the khabar (predicate) of إنهم.. ﴿وَماتُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined to the clause كفروا.. ﴿وَهُمْ فاسِقُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), with a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:85-85.t: This verse resembles verse 55, whose i'rab has already been given.

daas-irab:86-86.t:
﴿وَإِذا﴾ an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the wāw is resumptive. ﴿أُنْزِلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ marks the feminine. ﴿سُورَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming or explicative particle. ﴿آمِنُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by an implied preposition, i.e. "with belief in Allah", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb أنزلت. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to آمنوا. The clause ﴿أُنْزِلَتْ..﴾ is in the position of genitive by annexation. It has also been said that أن is explicative. ﴿وَجاهِدُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to the verb, and it is muḍāf. ﴿رَسُولِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿اسْتَأْذَنَكَ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿أُولُوا﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the nūn has been dropped because of annexation. ﴿الطَّوْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from أولو الطول. The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ conjoined to استأذنك. ﴿ذَرْنا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; نا is its object, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". ﴿نَكُنْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer of the command, and its ism (subject) is "we". ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿الْقاعِدِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:87-87.t: ﴿رَضُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أن﴾ subjunctive-making. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its ism (subject); it is subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of its subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, i.e. "they were content with their being.." ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْخَوالِفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَطُبِعَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the fāʾ is resumptive; the clause ﴿لا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ is the khabar, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:88-88.t:
﴿لكِنِ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun conjoined to الرسول, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause ﴿جاهَدُوا..﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الخيرات.
﴿الْخَيْراتُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause لهم الخيرات is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ conjoined to the resumptive clause أولئك لهم الخيرات, so it is like it.

daas-irab:89-89.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa, a sound feminine plural. The clause is resumptive. ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ are attached. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as a naʿt (adjective). [Translator's note: so in the source; since جنات is accusative here, the naʿt clause would be in the position of accusative.] ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to خالدين. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ naʿt. The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:90-90.t: ﴿وَجاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنَ الْأَعْرابِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِيُؤْذَنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by the implied أن after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb جاء. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿وَقَعَدَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined, and the clause ﴿كَذَبُوا اللَّهَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, the sīn denoting the future, and the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: so in the source; يصيب is an imperfect verb.] The clause ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:91-91.t:
﴿لَيْسَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عَلَى الضُّعَفاءِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿وَلا عَلَى الْمَرْضى، وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) nouns. ﴿لا يَجِدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); لا is negating and without governing effect. The relative noun ﴿ما﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لا يجدون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and likewise the clause ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾.
﴿حَرَجٌ﴾ the ism (subject) of laysa. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb for future time.. and the clause ﴿نَصَحُوا﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation.
﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the preposition and the Name of Majesty are attached to the verb. ﴿ما عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and ما is negating and without governing effect. ﴿مِنْ سَبِيلٍ﴾ من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿سَبِيلٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ, with its two khabars, and the clause is likewise resumptive.

daas-irab:92-92.t:
﴿وَلا عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the previous verse. ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial.. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿أَتَوْكَ﴾ the verbal clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by the implied أن after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أتوك.. ﴿قُلْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد assumed before it; the clause تولوا is thus the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).. ﴿لا أَجِدُ ما﴾ an imperfect verb, and the relative noun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَحْمِلُكُمْ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the hāʾ is in the position of genitive by annexation, the mīm marks the masculine plural, the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is circumstantial. The clause ﴿تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar (predicate). ﴿حَزَناً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿أَلَّا﴾ أن is a maṣdar-forming, subjunctive-making particle, and لا is negating. ﴿يَجِدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of its subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, i.e. "for not finding what they could spend", and the two are attached to ﴿حَزَناً﴾. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what they spend (it)".
[Part Two]
[Continuation of Surat al-Tawba]

daas-irab:93-93.t:
﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿السَّبِيلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is resumptive.
﴿يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿وَهُمْ أَغْنِياءُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿رَضُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, with قد assumed before it. ﴿بِأَنْ﴾ أن is subjunctive-making. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, subjunctive, and the wāw is its ism (subject); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to رضوا. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to the omitted khabar of يكونوا. ﴿الْخَوالِفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ the verbal clause is conjoined. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ is a conjunction. The clause ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is its khabar, and the clause ﴿فَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:94-94.t: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial, conditional, non-jussive. ﴿رَجَعْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لا﴾ the jussive-making lā of prohibition. ﴿تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَنْ﴾ a subjunctive-making particle. ﴿نُؤْمِنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to نؤمن, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿نَبَّأَنَا﴾ a past verb and its first object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, a delayed fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ أَخْبارِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted second object. ﴿وَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ﴾ a conjunction, the sīn denoting the future, the verb is imperfect, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿عَمَلَكُمْ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تُرَدُّونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿إِلى عالِمِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالشَّهادَةِ﴾ conjoined to الغيب. ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, an imperfect verb and its first object, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to the omitted second object. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its ism (subject), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

daas-irab:95-95.t: ﴿سَيَحْلِفُونَ﴾ the sīn denotes the future, an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِذَا﴾ adverbial, conditional, non-jussive. ﴿انْقَلَبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿لِتُعْرِضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation, subjunctive by the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿فَأَعْرِضُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its ism (subject). ﴿رِجْسٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the clause is causal. ﴿وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, with a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "يجزون". ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to جزاء. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its ism, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كنتم. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb here is كانوا.]

daas-irab:96-96.t: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to يحلفون, and the clause is a badal (substitute) of سيحلفون. ﴿لِتَرْضَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to ترضوا. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (indicating an implied condition), and إن is a jussive-making conditional particle. ﴿تَرْضَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to ترضوا. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna, and the Name of Majesty is its ism (subject), and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَرْضى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif owing to impossibility, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنِ الْقَوْمِ﴾ the two are attached to يرضى. ﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of القوم.

daas-irab:97-98.t: ﴿الْأَعْرابُ أَشَدُّ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). ﴿كُفْراً﴾ tamyīz (specification), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَنِفاقاً﴾ conjoined to كفرا. ﴿وَأَجْدَرُ﴾ conjoined to أشد. ﴿أَلَّا﴾ composed of the subjunctive-making أن and the negating لا. ﴿يَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); أن and what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿حُدُودَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ, with its two khabars, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿مِنَ﴾; the Quranic text reads ﴿مَنْ﴾.] ﴿يَتَّخِذُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يُنْفِقُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مَغْرَماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of يتخذ. ﴿وَيَتَرَبَّصُ﴾ conjoined to يتخذ and parsed like it. ﴿بِكُمُ﴾ the two are attached to يتربص. ﴿الدَّوائِرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿دائِرَةُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّوْءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, with a mubtadaʾ and its two khabars.

daas-irab:99-100.t: ﴿وَمِنَ الْأَعْرابِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ﴾ the i'rab of its like has already been given in the preceding verse. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to يؤمن. ﴿وَالْيَوْمِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الْآخِرِ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَتَّخِذُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُنْفِقُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿قُرُباتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place in the position of accusative as a naʿt of قربات. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَصَلَواتِ﴾ conjoined to قربات. ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of alerting (tanbīh). ﴿إِنَّها قُرْبَةٌ﴾ inna, its ism (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to قربة, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ the sīn denotes the future, an imperfect verb, the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يدخلهم, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its ism and its two khabars, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالسَّابِقُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿مِنَ الْمُهاجِرِينَ﴾ the two are attached to رضي. [Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase is more commonly taken as attached to an omitted ḥāl of السابقون.] ﴿وَالْأَنْصارِ﴾ conjoined to المهاجرين. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun conjoined to الأنصار. ﴿اتَّبَعُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of السابقون. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to رضي. ﴿وَرَضُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to رضوا. ﴿وَأَعَدَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to أعد. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿تَحْتَهَا﴾ the two are attached to تجري. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt of جنات. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to خالدين. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time attached to خالدين. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; the lām denotes distance and the kāf is for address, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ naʿt.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿بَراءَةٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذه براءة" (this is a declaration of disavowal). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of براءة. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective. ﴿عاهَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb. The clause هذه براءة is initial and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فَسِيحُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and likewise the adverb of time ﴿أَرْبَعَةَ﴾ is attached to the verb. ﴿أَشْهُرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾ أنّ, and the kāf is its noun and the mīm is for the masculine plural; and ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ is khabar (predicate). ﴿مُعْجِزِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural, the nūn having been dropped for the construct; and the yāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿مُخْزِي﴾ its khabar, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness. ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar formed from أنّ with its noun and its khabar is conjoined and stands in place of the two objects of علم.

daas-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وَأَذانٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذا أذان" (this is a proclamation). The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿إِلَى النَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the khabar, and likewise the adverb ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ is attached to it. ﴿الْحَجِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْأَكْبَرِ﴾ adjective (ṣifa). ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ﴾ أنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun and بريء is its khabar. ﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to بريء; the interpreted maṣdar formed from أنّ with its noun and its khabar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أذان. [Translator's note: the bāʾ is not written in the verse; the source treats it as implied (بأنّ).] ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "ورسوله بريء" (and His Messenger is free of them).. The clause is conjoined. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive, and the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿تُبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is joined to the tāʾ of the agent; it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is linking, and هم is a detached nominative pronoun, mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints هم; the pronoun in the verse is هو.] ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ its khabar. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا﴾ parsed like the preceding one. ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾ أنّ, and the kāf is its noun. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ khabar.. and أنّ with its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of ﴿اعلموا﴾. ﴿مُعْجِزِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبَشِّرِ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "أنت". ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾
the relative noun is its object. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb كفروا, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. [Translator's note: so in the source; بعذاب is normally attached to بشّر, and the ṣila is كفروا alone.] ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ adjective; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative by exception. ﴿عاهَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past). ﴿يَنْقُصُوكُمْ﴾ a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object.
﴿شَيْئاً﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf), and likewise the clause ﴿وَلَمْ يُظاهِرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَحَداً﴾. ﴿فَأَتِمُّوا إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلى مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the verbal clause ﴿يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is causal or resumptive.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَإِذَا﴾ an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and put in the accusative by its apodosis; the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿انْسَلَخَ الْأَشْهُرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْحُرُمُ﴾ adjective (ṣifa). ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a condition that does not put the verb in the jussive. ﴿الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿حَيْثُ﴾ an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اقتلوا. ﴿وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn because it is joined to the tāʾ of the agent, and the tāʾ is a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil. The ḍamma of the mīm has been lengthened. ﴿وَخُذُوهُمْ﴾ an imperative, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَاحْصُرُوهُمْ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَاقْعُدُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مَرْصَدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ إن is conditional. ﴿تابُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَخَلُّوا﴾ the fāʾ is linking, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿سَبِيلَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun, and غفور رحيم are its two khabars (predicates).
