They were pleased with their great numbers, so Allah made their punishment for being pleased with their numbers, and for their saying "We will not be overcome today for lack of numbers," that He struck them with terror until they turned back in flight, and none remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb «[Translator's note: so in the text; the reports usually name Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.]». Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon them until they returned and were victorious; and on that day Allah showed them of His signs that which increased them in clear evidence of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ.
His words: ﴿إنَّما يَعْمُرُ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 18] — it has also been read "مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ". Whoever reads "مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ" means by it the Sacred Mosque, with others included along with it, as you say: "How easy it is for so-and-so to spend the dirham and the dinar!", that is: spending this kind is easy for him. It is also possible that by "مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ" the Sacred Mosque is meant, as you say, when a man rides a horse: "So-and-so has taken to riding horses." Nouns that express genera run on this basis.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His words: ﴿إنَّما المُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلا يَقْرَبُوا المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ بَعْدَ عامِهِمْ هَذا﴾ — "نَجَسٌ" is said of everything regarded as filthy; and when you mention "اَلرِّجْسَ" you say: "هو رِجْسٌ نَجِسٌ". This took place in the year nine of the Hijra: the Muslims were commanded to prevent the idolaters from the Ḥajj and to kill them wherever they came upon them. ﴿وَإنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ إنْ شاءَ﴾ — the people of Mecca had a source of earnings and benefit from those of the idolaters who used to perform the pilgrimage, so Allah made known to them that He would compensate them for that. "اَلْعَيْلَةُ" is poverty. The poet said:
وَما يَدْرِي الفَقِيرُ مَتى غِناهُ ∗∗∗ وما يَدْرِي الغَنِيُّ مَتى يَعِيلُ
(The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor.)

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ولا بِاليَوْمِ الآخِرِ ولا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ﴾ — its meaning is: those who do not believe in Allah with the faith of those who affirm His oneness; for they acknowledged that Allah is their Creator, and that He has a son, and the idolaters associated idols with Him. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic — made known that this is not faith in Allah, and that their belief in the resurrection is not of the kind of our belief, because they do not acknowledge that the people of Paradise eat and drink; so they do not acknowledge the Last Day as Allah — Majestic and Mighty — has made it known, and they do not follow the religion of truth. So Allah commanded the killing of the disbelievers all together, unless they give the jizya out of hand; and accepting the jizya was made obligatory from the People of the Book, namely the Christians and the Jews.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laid down as a sunna regarding the Magians and the Sabians that they be treated like the People of the Book in the acceptance of the jizya. As for the idol-worshippers among the Arabs, for them there is nothing but killing, and likewise for others besides them.
His words: ﴿حَتّى يُعْطُوا الجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وهم صاغِرُونَ﴾ — it was said that the meaning of "عَنْ يَدٍ" is: out of abasement. It was said: "عَنْ يَدٍ" means out of subjugation and abasement, as you say: "اَلْيَدُ في هَذا لِفُلانٍ" (the hand in this belongs to so-and-so), that is: the effective command belongs to so-and-so. And it was said: "عَنْ يَدٍ", that is: as a favour bestowed on them thereby, because accepting the jizya from them and leaving them alive is a favour to them and an abundant act (yad) of kindness.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His words: ﴿وَقالَتِ اليَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ وقالَتِ النَّصارى المَسِيحُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ﴾ — "عُزَيْرُ" has been read with tanwīn and without tanwīn. The proper way is to keep the tanwīn, because "اِبْنُ" is the khabar (predicate); the tanwīn is dropped only with the adjective, as in your saying "جاءَنِي زَيْدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو" (Zayd son of ʿAmr came to me): the tanwīn is dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, because "اِبْنُ" is in genitive construct with a proper name, and because the adjective and the thing qualified are like a single thing. But when it is a khabar, then the tanwīn is kept. Dropping the tanwīn is sometimes permissible — weakly — because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; it has been read "قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدُ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ" with the tanwīn dropped because of its being vowelless together with the vowellessness of the bāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the text; the vowelless letter following is the lām of اللَّه here, and the bāʾ of ابن in the case of عُزَيْرُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ.]» in His words "عُزَيْرُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ". There is another way in it: that the khabar is omitted, so that its meaning is: "Uzayr son of Allah is the one we worship," in which case "اِبْنُ" is a naʿt (adjective). There is no disagreement among the grammarians that keeping the tanwīn is better.
His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهم بِأفْواهِهِمْ﴾ — if someone says: every saying is with the mouth, so what is the benefit of His saying "with their mouths"? The benefit in it is great and clear: the meaning is that there is no clear proof or demonstration in it; it is only a saying with the mouth, with no sound meaning beneath it, because they acknowledge that Allah has not taken a consort, so how can they claim a son for Him? It is only lying and mere talk.
His words: ﴿يُضاهِئُونَ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: in this saying of theirs they resemble those of their disbelievers who preceded them; that is: they said it only in imitation of those of their disbelievers who preceded them. The evidence for that is His words: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أحْبارَهم ورُهْبانَهم أرْبابًا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 31], that is: they accepted from them that ʿUzayr and the Messiah are the two sons of Allah the Exalted; and this is the meaning of "يُضاهِئُونَ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن قَبْلُ". It has also been read "يُضاهُونَ". The root meaning of "اَلْمُضاهاةُ" in the language is resemblance, and leaving out the hamza is more common. Its derivation is from their saying "اِمْرَأةٌ ضَهْياءُ", a woman who grows no breasts; it was also said: one who does not menstruate. Its meaning is only that she resembles men in having no breasts, and likewise if she does not menstruate. "ضَهْياءُ" is on the pattern فَعْلاءُ, the hamza being augmentative (zāʾida), as it is augmented in "شَمْألُ" (north wind) and "غِرْقِيءُ البَيْضَةِ" (the inner membrane of the egg); we do not know of it being augmented in other than initial position except in these words. It is also possible that it is "فَعْيَلٌ", even though it is a pattern that has no parallel in the language, for we know many things that have no second, among them their word "كَنَهْبَلٌ", which is large trees, whose measure is "فَنَعْلَلٌ"; likewise "قَرَنْفُلٌ" (clove) has no parallel, and its measure is "فَعَنْلُلٌ". It has also been said that "إبِلٌ" has no parallel, even though "إطِلٌ" occurs, which is the flank; they said "إيْطِلٌ" and then shortened it and said "إطِلٌ". So it is possible that "يُضاهِئُونَ", with hamza, is from this, and that the hamza of "ضَهْياءُ" is a radical hamza.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His words: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: declaring Him exalted above their shirk (associating partners).

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His words: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ والفِضَّةَ ولا يُنْفِقُونَها في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهم بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ — most of the exegesis takes it to refer to the idolaters, but it has also been said that it concerns those of the people of the qibla who withhold zakāt, because whoever pays the zakāt of his wealth has spent in the way of Allah what is due from his wealth.
His words: ﴿وَيَأْبى اللَّهُ إلا أنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ﴾ [al-Tawba: 32] — "إلّا" has entered although there is no negation in the speech. You do not say "ضَرَبْتُ إلّا زَيْدًا" (I struck except Zayd), because the speech gives no indication of what is omitted. But when you say ﴿وَيَأْبى اللَّهُ إلا أنْ يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ﴾ [al-Tawba: 32], the meaning is: "Allah refuses everything except that He perfect His light." Some grammarians claimed that "يَأْبى" contains an element of negation; but negation and affirmation do not have "elements". The instruments of negation are "لا", "ما", "لَمْ", "لَنْ" and "لَيْسَ"; these have no "elements" — they are pronounced as they are — and an affirmative cannot be a negation. If this were permissible on the grounds that it contains an element of negation, then "كَرِهْتُ إلّا أخاكَ" (I disliked except your brother) would be permissible, whereas there is no indication here of what is disliked, what it is or who it is. So "كَرِهْتُ" is like "أبَيْتُ", except that with "أبَيْتُ" the omission is in use.
His words: ﴿وَلا يُنْفِقُونَها في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — He said ﴿الذَّهَبَ والفِضَّةَ﴾ and did not say "وَلا يُنْفِقُونَهُما في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (with the dual pronoun). That is permissible only because the meaning is: "they hoard gold and silver and do not spend what is hoarded in the way of Allah." It is also possible that it is construed with reference to wealth, so that it is: "they do not spend it — they do not spend the wealth." It is also possible that "وَلا يُنْفِقُونَها" means "they do not spend the silver," and gold was omitted because it is included in the silver, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وأنْتَ بِما ∗∗∗ عِنْدَكَ راضٍ والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content — and opinion differs.)
He means: "We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have," and he omitted "راضُونَ". Likewise the meaning will be: "Those who hoard gold and do not spend it in the way of Allah, and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah."

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His words: ﴿إنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا في كِتابِ اللَّهِ﴾ — Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that the number of the months of the Muslims — who were bidden in worship to assign to their year — is twelve months according to the stations of the moon «[Translator's note: the relative clause is incomplete as transmitted.]». Their Ḥajj, their festivals and their prayer at their festivals were made according to this number, so the Ḥajj and the fast fall once in winter and once in summer, and in the different seasons, according to the months and the rotation of the years. The festivals and acts of worship of the People of the Book in their year were observed on the basis that the year is three hundred and sixty-five days and part of a day; on this the practice of the Christians and the Jews runs. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that the years of the Muslims are by the new moons.
His words: ﴿مِنها أرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ﴾ — the four sacred months are al-Muḥarram, Rajab, Dhū al-Qaʿda and Dhū al-Ḥijja. ﴿فَلا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — it was said: in the four; and it was said: in the twelve. Whoever said "in the four" said: He intended to stress the gravity of sins, as He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿فَلا رَفَثَ ولا فُسُوقَ ولا جِدالَ في الحَجِّ﴾ [al-Baqara: 197]; for wickedness is not permissible in the Ḥajj or outside it, but He — Mighty and Majestic — made known the days in which sins are greater in guilt and punishment.
His words: ﴿وَقاتِلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ كافَّةً كَما يُقاتِلُونَكم كافَّةً﴾ — "كافَّةً" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern "فاعِلَةً", just as they said "اَلْعاقِبَةُ" and "اَلْعافِيَةُ". It stands in the sense of "fight the idolaters, encompassing them with the resolve to fight them." It is derived from "كُفَّةُ الشَّيْءِ", the edge of a thing; it was taken from the fact that when a thing reaches that point it is held back (kuffa) from increasing. It may not be put in the dual or plural: one does not say "قاتِلُوهم كافّاتٍ" or "كافِّينَ", just as when you say "قاتِلُوهم عامَّةً" (fight them all together) you do not put it in the dual or plural, and likewise "خاصَّةً".
This is the school of the grammarians.
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ — its interpretation is that He guarantees them victory.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His words: ﴿إنَّما النَّسِيءُ زِيادَةٌ في الكُفْرِ﴾ — "اَلنَّسِيءُ" here is the postponement of a thing. They used to forbid fighting in al-Muḥarram; but when they resolved to fight in it, they made Ṣafar like al-Muḥarram, fought in al-Muḥarram, and substituted Ṣafar for it. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that this is an increase in disbelief. ﴿لِيُواطِئُوا عِدَّةَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ — so that they make Ṣafar like al-Muḥarram in the count, and say: "These are four in place of four." "اَلْمُواطَأةُ" is matching and agreeing on a thing.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿ما لَكم إذا قِيلَ لَكُمُ انْفِرُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اثّاقَلْتُمْ إلى الأرْضِ﴾ — the reports agree that this was in the expedition of Tabūk, and that is because the people went out on it in severe and arduous hardship.
His words — Mighty and Majestic —: ﴿اثّاقَلْتُمْ إلى الأرْضِ﴾ — the meaning is "تَثاقَلْتُمْ" (you became heavy), except that the tāʾ was assimilated into the tāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the text; what is meant is the assimilation of the tāʾ into the thāʾ.]» and became a vowelless thāʾ, so it was begun with the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) for the purpose of beginning.
In "اثّاقَلْتُمْ إلى الأرْضِ" there is, in my view, more than one way: among them that its meaning is "you inclined heavily towards staying in your land," and among them "you inclined heavily towards the desires of this world."
His words: ﴿أرَضِيتُمْ بِالحَياةِ الدُّنْيا مِنَ الآخِرَةِ﴾, that is: are you content with the bliss of the life of this world in place of the bliss of the Hereafter? ﴿فَما مَتاعُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا في الآخِرَةِ إلا قَلِيلٌ﴾, that is: what is enjoyed in this world is little compared to what the friends of Allah enjoy in Paradise.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His words: ﴿إلا تَنْفِرُوا يُعَذِّبْكم عَذابًا ألِيمًا ويَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ — this is a severe threat concerning staying behind from jihād. He made known that He will substitute, to support His religion and His Prophet, a people who are not sluggish in going out to give support against His enemies, since Allah — Mighty and Majestic — made known to them that if they abandon supporting him, that will not harm him at all, just as it did not harm him when he was in Mecca with no helpers. So He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿إلا تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إذْ أخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إذْ هُما في الغارِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 40].
«The idolaters had agreed to kill him ﷺ, so he and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq went off, fleeing from them by night, and he left ʿAlī on his bed so that they would see a person on the bed and not know the time of his departure. The two of them informed Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr of their place in the cave. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a thumāma, which is a small, weak shrub, and ordered Abū Bakr to take it with him. When they reached the cave, he ordered Abū Bakr, and he placed it at the entrance of the cave. Then Abū Bakr went ahead into the cave, lay flat in it and threw himself down. The Messenger of Allah said: "Why did you do that?" He said: "Because in these caves there are harmful creeping creatures and wild beasts, and I wanted, if there was anything in it, to shield you with myself, O Messenger of Allah." Abū Bakr saw a hole in the cave and blocked it with his foot, and said: "If something harmful comes out of it, I will have shielded you from it." When morning came, the idolaters passed by the cave, and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq wept. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "I fear that you will be killed and Allah will not be worshipped after today." The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Do not grieve; Allah is with us" — that is: Allah the Exalted will hold them back from us and help us. He said: "Is it so, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Then Abū Bakr's tears dried and he grew calm.» When the idolaters passed by the cave they said: "If anyone were in it, this thumāma would not be at its entrance." ﴿فَأنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وأيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْها﴾ [al-Tawba: 40] — He strengthened him with angels who turned the faces and eyes of the disbelievers away from seeing him.
His words: "سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ" — it is possible that the hāʾ in "عَلَيْهِ" refers to Abū Bakr, and it is possible that it refers back to the Prophet ﷺ, because Allah — glorious is His praise — cast into his heart that by which he was calmed, and he knew that they would not reach him. So Allah made known that if they abandoned supporting him, He would support him as He supported him in this situation. "ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "Allah supported him as one of two," that is: He supported him when he was alone except for Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him.

zajjaj:41-41.t: He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿انْفِرُوا خِفافًا وثِقالا وجاهِدُوا بِأمْوالِكم وأنْفُسِكُمْ﴾. It was said: "خِفافًا وثِقالًا" means: well-off and hard-pressed. It was said: "خِفافًا وثِقالًا": whether movement is light or heavy for you. It was said: riding and on foot. And it was also said: young and old. It is related «that Ibn Umm Maktūm came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Must I go out?" He said: "Yes" — until Allah — Mighty and Majestic — sent down: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلى الأعْمى حَرَجٌ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 17].»

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿لَوْ كانَ عَرَضًا قَرِيبًا وسَفَرًا قاصِدًا لاتَّبَعُوكَ﴾ — "اَلْعَرَضُ" is every worldly benefit that presents itself to you. So the meaning is: "If it had been nearby booty," that is: if what they were called to had been gain; and "سَفَرًا قاصِدًا", that is: an easy, short journey. ﴿لاتَّبَعُوكَ ولَكِنْ بَعُدَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّقَّةُ﴾, that is: the destination you were aiming for seemed far to them. This was when they were called to the expedition of Tabūk, and going out towards the regions of Syria was burdensome for them.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His words: ﴿عَفا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ لِمَ أذِنْتَ لَهم حَتّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وتَعْلَمَ الكاذِبِينَ﴾, that is: until it becomes clear to you who is a hypocrite and who is sincere.

zajjaj:44-44.t: Then He — Majestic and Exalted — made known to him that the sign of hypocrisy at that time was asking permission to be excused from jihād, and said: ﴿لا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ أنْ يُجاهِدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ﴾. The position of "أنْ" is accusative; the meaning is: these do not ask your permission regarding striving (في أنْ يُجاهِدُوا), but "في" was omitted, so the verb passed directly to it and put "أنْ" in the accusative. Sībawayh said: It is also possible that its position is genitive, because the omission of the preposition here was permitted only with "أنْ" being overt. If you made the maṣdar (verbal noun) overt, you would not omit "في" — "لا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ القَوْمُ الجِهادَ" — until you say "في الجِهادِ"; but "لا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ القَوْمُ أنْ يُجاهِدُوا" is permissible.

zajjaj:45-45.t: His words: ﴿إنَّما يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ وارْتابَتْ قُلُوبُهم فَهم في رَيْبِهِمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ﴾ — Allah — glorious is His praise — made known that whoever doubts and is uncertain about Allah and about the resurrection is a disbeliever.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
﴿وَلَوْ أرادُوا الخُرُوجَ لأعَدُّوا لَهُ عُدَّةً﴾, that is: their failure to make preparation is evidence of their intention to stay behind. ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَرِهَ اللَّهُ انْبِعاثَهم فَثَبَّطَهُمْ﴾ — "اَلتَّثْبِيطُ" is your turning a person back from something he is doing; that is: Allah disliked that they should go out with you, so He turned them back from going out. Then He — Mighty and Majestic — made known why He disliked that, and said: ﴿لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكم ما زادُوكم إلا خَبالا﴾ [al-Tawba: 47]. "اَلْخَبالُ" is corruption and the loss of a thing. The poet said:
أبَنِي لُبَيْنى لَسْتُما بِيَدٍ ∗∗∗ إلّا يَدًا مَخْبُولَةَ العَضُدِ
(O sons of Lubaynā, you two are no hand, except a hand whose upper arm is crippled.)
that is: with a corrupted upper arm. ﴿وَلأوْضَعُوا خِلالَكُمْ﴾ [al-Tawba: 47] — one says "أوْضَعْتُ في السَّيْرِ" when I hastened in travelling: "and they would have hastened in what would disrupt you." ﴿يَبْغُونَكُمُ الفِتْنَةَ وفِيكم سَمّاعُونَ لَهُمْ﴾ [al-Tawba: 47], that is: "among you are those who listen and convey to them what they want"; and it is possible that "سَمّاعُونَ لَهم" means those who accept from them.
In the muṣḥaf "ولَأوْضَعُوا" is written "ولَأ اوْضَعُوا", and similar to it in the Qur'an is "أوْ لَأ اذْبَحَنَّهُ", also with an extra alif. By its pronunciation this ought to be "ولَأوْضَعُوا"; but before "the Arabic" the fatḥa used to be written as an alif, and writing in "the Arabic" was begun close to the revelation of the Qur'an, so additions occurred in it in places, and things were followed with letters lacking. So "ولا أوْضَعُوا" was written with a lām and an alif — in place of the fatḥa — and with a hamza. This is the explanation of what has occurred of this kind in the written text.

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿وَمِنهم مَن يَقُولُ ائْذَنْ لِي ولا تَفْتِنِّي﴾, that is: do not make me sinful by commanding me to go out when that is not easy for me, so that I would sin. It was also said that the hypocrites mocked the Muslims during the expedition of Tabūk, saying: "Are you after the daughters of al-Aṣfar (the Byzantines)?" So he said: "لا تَفْتِنِّي", that is: do not tempt me with the daughters of al-Aṣfar. So Allah the Exalted made known that they had already fallen into fitna (temptation), that is: they had fallen into sin.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿إنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهم وإنْ تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ يَقُولُوا قَدْ أخَذْنا أمْرَنا مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: we knew the prudent course in staying behind from you. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty — made known that nothing will befall the Muslims except what Allah has written for them, and He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنا إلا ما كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنا﴾ [al-Tawba: 51], that is: what He has decreed for us, as He said: ﴿ما أصابَ مِن مُصِيبَةٍ في الأرْضِ ولا في أنْفُسِكم إلا في كِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَبْرَأها﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 22]; then He reinforced that, saying: ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ عَلى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 22]. There is another way in it: "Nothing will befall us except what Allah has written for us — what He has made clear to us in His Book — namely that either we are victorious, and that will be a good outcome for us, or we are killed, and martyrdom will also be a good outcome for us"; that is: Allah has written for us what befalls us, or: we have known what share we have in it. Then He — glorious is His praise — made it clear, and the Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنا إلا إحْدى الحُسْنَيَيْنِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 52] — only victory or martyrdom — ﴿وَنَحْنُ نَتَرَبَّصُ بِكم أنْ يُصِيبَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابٍ مِن عِنْدِهِ أوْ بِأيْدِينا﴾ [al-Tawba: 52]. So you await for us one of the two best things, and we await for you one of the two evils; between what you await and what we await there is a great difference.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His words — Majestic and Mighty —: ﴿قُلْ أنْفِقُوا طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا﴾ — or if you wish, "كُرْهًا" with ḍamma. This is imperative in wording, but its meaning is that of condition and apodosis; the meaning is: whether you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Similar to this in poetry is the saying of Kuthayyir:
أسِيئِي بِنا أوْ أحْسِنِي لا مَلُومَةً ∗∗∗ لَدَيْنا ولا مَقْلِيَّةً إنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well — you are not blamed by us, nor hated, even if you turn to hate.)
He did not command her to treat him ill; rather he informed her that whether she treated him ill or well, he remained true to his pledge to her.
If someone says: How is the statement (khabar) in the sense of the command? «[Translator's note: so in the text; the case under discussion is a command in the sense of a statement/condition, and the reply gives the converse example.]» We say: it is like your saying "غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لِزَيْدٍ" (Allah forgave Zayd) and "رَحِمَ اللَّهُ زَيْدًا" (Allah had mercy on Zayd), whose meaning is: "O Allah, have mercy on Zayd."

zajjaj:54-54.t:
﴿وَما مَنَعَهم أنْ تُقْبَلَ مِنهم نَفَقاتُهم إلا أنَّهم كَفَرُوا﴾ — the position of the first "أنْ" is accusative, and the position of the second "أنْ" is nominative; the meaning is: nothing prevented the acceptance of their spending except their disbelief. "أنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنهم نَفَقاتُهم" (with the masculine verb) is permissible, because "نَفَقاتُ" has the sense of "إنْفاقُ" (spending). "وَما مَنَعَهم مِن أنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنهم نَفَقاتُهم إلّا أنَّهم كَفَرُوا" is also permissible, but it is not permissible to read it so, because it has not been transmitted as a reading.
His words: ﴿وَلا يَأْتُونَ الصَّلاةَ إلا وهم كُسالى﴾ — also "كَسالى"; with ḍamma and fatḥa it is the plural of "كَسْلانُ", like your saying "سَكْرانُ", "سُكارى" and "سَكارى". "وَلا يَأْتُونَ الصَّلاةَ إلّا وهم كَسْلى" is also permissible, but that is not permissible in the Qur'an. ﴿وَلا يُنْفِقُونَ إلا وهم كارِهُونَ﴾ — the reading is with fatḥa on the kāf; kasra is also possible: "إلّا وهم كِارِهُونَ", but it has not been transmitted in the Qur'an. «[Translator's note: so in the text: كارهون has an alif after the kāf; the remark presumably refers to the vowelling of the kāf as given.]»

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His words: ﴿فَلا تُعْجِبْكَ أمْوالُهم ولا أوْلادُهم إنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهم بِها في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ — its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Let not their wealth and their children in this world impress you; Allah only intends to punish them with them in the Hereafter." It is also possible — and Allah knows best —: "Allah only intends to punish them with them in this world," that is: "they spend it in this world while they are hypocrites, so they are tormented by spending it, since they spend it unwillingly."
His words: ﴿وَتَزْهَقَ أنْفُسُهم وهم كافِرُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "and their souls depart," that is: what is hateful to them becomes so severe for them that their souls depart.

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إنَّهم لَمِنكم وما هم مِنكُمْ﴾, that is: they swear by Allah that they are believers just as you are believers, but they are not of you, because they display faith and conceal disbelief. ﴿وَلَكِنَّهم قَوْمٌ يَفْرَقُونَ﴾, that is: "they are afraid to reveal what they really are, lest they be killed."

zajjaj:57-57.t:
Then He — Majestic and Mighty — made known that if they found a way of escape in it, they would part from you, and He — Majestic and Mighty — said: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً أوْ مَغاراتٍ﴾. "المَلْجَأُ" and "اَللَّجَأُ" — the latter with short final vowel and hamza — is the place in which one takes refuge. "مَغاراتٌ" is the plural of "مَغارَةٌ", the place into which a person sinks (يَغُورُ), that is: in which he hides. It is also read "أوْ مُغاراتٍ" with ḍamma on the mīm, because one says "أغَرْتُ" and "غُرْتُ" when I have entered low ground (al-ghawr).
His words: ﴿أوْ مُدَّخَلا﴾ — it is also read "أوْ مُدْخَلًا" without doubling, and it is read "أوْ مَدْخَلًا". As for "مُدَّخَلٌ", its origin is "مُدْتَخَلٌ"; but the tāʾ and the dāl are from one place of articulation, so it was lighter for the speech to be from a single point. Whoever says "مَدْخَلًا" takes it from "دَخَلَ، يَدْخُلُ، مَدْخَلًا"; and whoever says "مُدْخَلًا" takes it from "أدْخَلْتُهُ مُدْخَلًا". The poet said:
اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ مُمْسانا ومُصْبَحَنا ∗∗∗ بِالخَيْرِ صَبَّحَنا رَبِّي ومَسّانا
(Praise be to Allah for our evening and our morning; with good my Lord has brought us morning and evening.)
The meaning of "مُدَّخَلٌ" and "مُدْخَلٌ" is: if they found a people whose company they could enter, or who would bring them into their company. ﴿لَوَلَّوْا إلَيْهِ وهم يَجْمَحُونَ﴾ — the meaning is: if they found these things, "they would turn to it, bolting," that is: hastening with a haste that nothing can turn their faces back from. From this is said "فَرَسٌ جُمُوحٌ" (a bolting horse) of the one which, when it charges, the bridle cannot hold back.
